scope: Four complementary foundational figures: current MCS scientific director, his external doctoral adviser, and historical PDMI mathematical physics lineage.

people.name: Stanislav Smirnov
people.status: Principal researcher · Scientific director of MCS
people.interests: Probability, mathematical physics, complex analysis and dynamical systems.

sources.title: Stanislav Smirnov: own CV at Academia Europaea (2013)

people.notes: Current MCS directory explicitly lists principal researcher and scientific director; it does not currently use the title professor. His 1996 PhD advisor was Nikolai Makarov. His own CV identifies Victor Havin separately as adviser of his 1992 St. Petersburg undergraduate/master’s work.

people.name: Nikolai Makarov
people.interests: Complex and harmonic analysis, potential theory, conformal field theory and random matrices.
people.notes: Richard Merkin Distinguished Professor at Caltech. Included as Smirnov’s doctoral adviser and a Leningrad University/LOMI alumnus; no current SPbSU or PDMI appointment is claimed.

people.name: Ludwig Faddeev
people.interests: Quantum scattering, gauge field theory, integrable systems and quantum groups.

sources.title: Arefeva, Semenov-Tian-Shansky and Takhtajan: Faddeev obituary (EMS, 2017)
Interview with Ludwig Faddeev (EMS Newsletter, June 2007), pp. 31–37

people.notes: 1934–2017. Historical head of the PDMI Laboratory of Mathematical Problems in Physics. PhD supervision by Olga Ladyzhenskaya is explicit in his own 2007 interview and the 2017 EMS obituary.

people.name: Olga Ladyzhenskaya
people.interests: Nonlinear partial differential equations, Navier–Stokes equations and mathematical hydrodynamics.

sources.title: St. Petersburg Mathematical Society: Olga Ladyzhenskaya

people.notes: 1922–2004. Joined Leningrad University after her 1949 PhD and the Steklov Institute in 1954; headed its Laboratory of Mathematical Physics from 1962. Sources differ on the Doctor of Sciences year (1953/1954), so no year is asserted.

sources.title: Stanislav Smirnov: own CV at Academia Europaea (2013)

links.notes: Caltech PhD: Spectral analysis of Julia sets; MCS gives May 1996, CV period concludes June 1996. Both explicitly name Nikolai Makarov as adviser.

links.notes: BSc/MSc adviser at St. Petersburg State University, 1987–1992, explicitly listed in Smirnov’s own CV. This is pre-doctoral supervision, not a second PhD adviser.

sources.title: Interview with Ludwig Faddeev (EMS Newsletter, June 2007), pp. 31–37
Arefeva, Semenov-Tian-Shansky and Takhtajan: Faddeev obituary (EMS, 2017)

links.notes: Faddeev’s own interview says Ladyzhenskaya remained his scientific supervisor during his research-student work on quantum inverse scattering. The 2017 obituary explicitly identifies her as thesis adviser during his PhD studentship at LOMI.

links.label: Mathematical mentor (self-described)

sources.title: Semenov-Tian-Shansky: Scattering on Riemannian symmetric spaces and Huygens principle (author-uploaded text, 2018)

links.notes: Optional mentorship edge only: Semenov-Tian-Shansky dedicates his own 2018 article to the memory of his teachers Faddeev and Pavlov. This establishes a self-described mathematical teacher; it does not by itself establish formal PhD or research supervision. Do not relabel as doctoral.

notes: IDs khavin and semenov-tian-shansky refer to people supplied by the other research files.
